subQuests.subQuestName: Head to the location of the Fatui machine

400771101.text: Hey, look! Isn't that the same guy we saw on our first day here?

400771102.text: Ahaha... *hic* Everyone's gone crazy. Everyone should get out of here!

400771103.text: We'll... We'll never wake up... But I was right, my precious, you are invincible... hehe...

400771105.text: A miracle machine... Definitely not... impossible... *hic*!

400771106.text: I think he's referring to that machine.

400771108.text: Oh goodness, the smell of alcohol... Mein Fräulein, please allow me to fan the fumes away with my wings.

400771109.text: Excellent, please fan them away for me, too.

400771112.text: I've checked the surroundings, but there's no one else here.

400771113.text: Isn't that strange? The Fatui is a big organization, but he is the only one left at this camp. What's more, we didn't even see him the last time we were here.

400771114.text: Even the larger gentleman from the first time is missing. I think... they must be hiding somewhere.

400771115.text: As for why they may be hiding, I'm afraid we'll have to ask him.

400771116.text: But he's as drunk as Tone-Deaf Bard... Should we wait for him to sober up?

400771117.text: Cleanse him with the holy spring of punishment!

400771118.text: Mein Fräulein means to splash him with water.

400771119.text: Sounds like a good idea. Let's try!

400771120.text: Everyone takes out their water bottles and empties them over the collapsed Fatui researcher...

400771123.text: Hey, are you one of the Fatui? Can you tell us what happened here and what that machine is for?

400771126.text: Oh... those blockheads from the administration will regret it now! Haha! That's what you get for rejecting my research and forcing me to...

400771127.text: Forcing me to... to conduct my research on this deserted island... My precious! My precious... *sobs*

400771128.text: Why is he crying? Looks like he has a lot of pent-up emotions...

400771129.text: ...You mocked me... and my precious invention! You... you don't know anything about the future.

400771130.text: Only my invention... can help us conquer the world! Haha... hahaha...

400771132.text: Ow! Don't hit me! I won't blow up the lab again... I'm sorry! I didn't mean to...

400771133.text: This man's gone insane. There's no way we can communicate with him.

400771134.text: He wasn't like this when we first met him. It looks like the effects have grown worse, to the point of driving him mad.

400771135.text: *sobs*... My manuscript, my manuscript! Only that... can save... save... *sobs*

400771137.text: Don't yell at me, don't yell at me... *sobs*

400771141.text: Kind sir, look at me. Now tell me, where did you hide your manuscript?

400771142.text: *sobs* No, no, don't force me to write a report... *sobs* Go away...

400771143.text: Ugh, he's completely lost in his own imagination...

400771147.text: Kazuha stands quietly for a while, then throws the researcher over his shoulder and onto the ground.

400771149.text: *sobs* Ow! My butt... *sobs* My brain is finally starting to work again... It's not a mushy mess anymore...

400771150.text: Can you tell me where you put the manuscript?

400771151.text: The manuscript... the manuscript... is in the crack over there...

400771152.text: Whew, finally! Otherwise, I was gonna have to blast some of my loudest rock 'n' roll in his ears.

400771153.text: Kazuha hesitated for a long time before making a move. He's so nice.

400771155.text: Everyone, let's search the stone cracks nearby for the manuscript.

400770102.text: Congratulations! We've found the key to solving the problem!

400770104.text: Mona takes the manuscript and studies it carefully...

400770105.text: Just as I thought. This machinery named "Cognitive Mimicry" is capable of altering the state of people's brains. It was invented by the researcher we met earlier, his name is Persikov.

400770106.text: According to the manuscript, the Fatui officials did not support Persikov's research. They believed he had taken the wrong path.

400770107.text: But Persikov insisted on putting his machine to use. In order to achieve that, he disassembled the machine and used his connections to transport the parts to this deserted island.

400770108.text: How did they find this island? The Fatui's intelligence network's not to be underestimated.

400770109.text: Persikov was dead set on carrying out his experiments on this island. Most of his subjects were junior Fatui soldiers who all signed a waiver before the experiment.

400770110.text: ...It looks like they really thought this machine would benefit the Fatui.

400770112.text: That's most likely top-secret. The manuscript didn't reveal any details, but Persikov did mention that the machine was modeled after the power of a god.

400770113.text: Does that mean... there's a god connected to these dream-like mirages, and the Fatui found a way to research it?

400770114.text: Clearly. Otherwise, they wouldn't have been able to reproduce the god's power.

400770115.text: (Wait, so there's some sort of... Mirage Archon?)

400770116.text: Anyway, Persikov's experiment did not go as planned. The machine broke down just days after it was activated. They tried to fix it, but...

400770117.text: The technologically illiterate Fatui soldiers completely ruined the machine. Even its most important component of all — the crystalline cores — got ejected and disappeared.

400770118.text: A testament to the importance of maintenance in all aspects of life. I believe we can all learn something from this.

400770119.text: Persikov may be a mad scientist, but he didn't want to see his subordinates suffer. Besides, if he didn't solve the problem, he would end up going insane as well.

400770120.text: As a last resort, Persikov went out on his own to look for the cores. But he was just a sickly researcher unfit for the task. He had to give up.

400770121.text: Then, Persikov went searching for the soldiers who had gone mad and strayed from the group, and took them to a hidden cave.

400770122.text: I think that was where they were at the day we arrived on this island. Persikov was taking a strong Fatui soldier somewhere.

400770123.text: Yes. It took Persikov all of his strength to get all the missing soldiers into the cave. He tried to snap them out of it with music and poetry...

400770125.text: We came here once but there was no one around. Come to think of it, that must've been the day Persikov was busy gathering the soldiers into the cave.

400770126.text: There's good news and bad news written on the last few pages.

400770127.text: The good news is, Persikov managed to figure out the location of the crystalline cores by piecing together the snippets of information he could get from the delirious soldiers...

400770128.text: The bad news is, Persikov failed to revive them, and eventually succumbed to the device's influence himself. The last few pages of the manuscript are just unintelligible drunken scribbles.

400770129.text: It appears that the responsibility for this issue now falls to my retainers and I.

400770132.text: There's a map in the manuscript. The markings should indicate the locations of the crystalline cores.

400770133.text: We've got no choice but to find the crystalline cores now!

400770201.text: (The researcher came to his senses briefly after Kazuha's throw, but soon fell unconscious...)

400770202.text: (Did his mental state deteriorate, or did Kazuha knock him out...?)

subQuests.subQuestName: Insert the Crystalline Cores into the machine

400770701.text: We've inserted all the crystalline cores. Mona, is that all we needed to do?

400770702.text: I think so. That's what the manuscript says anyway.

400770703.text: Let's give it some time. Hopefully, it'll return to normal.

400770704.text: Everyone sits around the campfire, chatting and cooking barbecue.

400770705.text: Once the machine is fixed, the situation seems to improve. Soon, you hear footsteps approaching...

400770708.text: Hold on, look at the machine... is it fixed?

400770709.text: What? But Mr. Persikov is still lying on the ground over there.

400770710.text: We're the ones who fixed the device. Yeah, you're welcome!

400770711.text: We could have had a nice, relaxing vacation, if all of this hadn't ended up occupying so much of our time.

400770712.text: Hmph! Apologize to me and my retainers at once!

400770713.text: Huh!? Oh no, oh no, I—I'm outta here...

400770714.text: Hey, hey! Don't leave me here on my own... Mr. Persikov's still there, we need to save him!

400770715.text: Haha, those two definitely seem a little more lucid now.

400770717.text: Yay! Let's get outta here then. Paimon wants to spend the rest of this vacation back at our own camp.

400770719.text: Yeah! But it feels like our camp now, kinda like our temporary home, hehe.

400770720.text: Then perhaps we should call it the Embassy of the Immernachtreich and Dodoland.

400770721.text: Huh? No! That's too many words. Paimon would prefer something easy to remember.

400770722.text: Come on, let's go home now.

400770801.text: *yawn* Whew! After coming home to a nice big meal then having a long lie down, Paimon's finally starting to feel relaxed.

400770802.text: Hehe, is the hospitality of the Immernachtreich to thy liking?

400770804.text: Wonderful. Mein Fräulein invited you all here not only to witness the arrival of our Holy Land, but most importantly, she wished that you could all relax and enjoy the summer.

400770805.text: Great! Well, I've come to the right place — I love it here!

400770806.text: May this place become an eternal paradise.

400770807.text: Mein Fräulein says she hopes to go on more adventures with you here in the future.

400770808.text: Of course! And you should come find me in Liyue when you get the time. I'll show you around.

400770809.text: Oh, also, my friend runs the best restaurant in Liyue. I'm sure you'll love it.

400770810.text: If you're into opera, you should go see Yun Jin. She's the nicest person, and she likes making friends with new and interesting people. I'm sure the two of you will have plenty to talk about with your shared passion for theatrics.

400770811.text: Oh? If Lady Xinyan speaks so highly of it, then I must entertain the idea.

400770813.text: There is a snack called Roasted Lavender Melon in Inazuma, which goes rather well with fish. Why don't we roast some fruit and seafood for dinner tonight?

400770815.text: Then it's decided. I'll go gather some more fruit. And for seasoning... Yup, that should do it.

400770824.text: I've noticed an issue. Although we've fixed the machine, as you can see — the mirages on the islands have still not disappeared.

400770825.text: I've noticed that, too. But considering it took some time for the mirages to appear, it may also take some time for them to disappear.

400770827.text: In other news, my scryglass seems to be working fine now. The divination results are also looking about right, although...

400770829.text: Although there are some parts in the results that I don't quite understand... it's as if there is some sort of power surrounding us, and it's still watching us.

400770830.text: Do you think it's caused by the machine, or perhaps Persikov?

400770831.text: Sorry, I'm also not sure. All I know is that the power is not hostile at the moment. Whatever it is, it doesn't seem to harbor any ill will toward us.

400770832.text: (That reminds me, there's one unanswered question on these islands. But the group is unaware.)

400770834.text: Well, although there's nothing left to disturb us, and we can finally kick back and enjoy our vacation, we still ought to be cautious while we're on these islands.

400770835.text: I will keep seeing what the stars say every day.

400770836.text: I promised Fischl that I'd be her guard. I can help.

400770837.text: Good, I'll be counting on you.

400770838.text: ...*sigh* Goodness knows why those girls are so carefree about everything. I suppose it falls to me to be extra vigilant.

400770842.text: Ohh, so we're gonna call the Tone-Deaf Bard, right?

400770844.text: Well hello there, strangers! You finally called! I thought you were having so much fun that you'd completely forgotten about me.

400770845.text: Nope! Tone-Deaf Bard, a whole bunch of really strange things happened!

400770846.text: You tell Venti everything that has happened on the islands over the past few days...

400770847.text: A strange machine that can imitate the power of a God? Wow, haha, I didn't know the Fatui had plans like that. Their imaginations are truly running wild.

400770848.text: So judging from your tone, it sounds like you don't know any more about this than we do?

400770849.text: Alas, I am but a humble bard who sings for his Mora in the tavern. Why would I know anything about it?

400770851.text: But, other than that, did you two have fun?

400770852.text: We did! We ate a lot of yummy food and saw loads of amazing things. It was really cool!

400770817.text: Oh? Did you try it in Inazuma?

400770818.text: A few Inazuman friends made some for me.

400770820.text: You know, I want to follow your example and travel around the world. Hopefully, I can also make good friends along the way.

400770821.text: Knowing you, that shouldn't be a problem.

400770822.text: #That means a lot coming from you, {NICKNAME}.

400779901.text: This should be one of the crystalline cores mentioned in the manuscript!
